title: Try one representative task
purpose: Create evidence for a task on your own map.
text:
I want to test your help with this task: {{taskName}}.
The purpose is {{goal}}, for {{audience}}.
Use these permitted inputs: {{approvedInputs}}.
Respect these constraints: {{constraints}}.
Return this deliverable: {{deliverable}}.
I will evaluate it against these criteria: {{successCriteria}}.
Identify missing information and distinguish supported claims from assumptions. If the task needs tools you cannot use, say which part you cannot complete. Produce the work so I can evaluate it; a plan alone is insufficient.

title: Delegate with a clear assignment
purpose: Define an agent assignment after checking that delegation is appropriate.
text:
Complete this assignment: {{goal}}.
Relevant context: {{context}}.
You may work within: {{allowedScope}}.
Leave these actions and decisions to me: {{limits}}.
Required deliverables: {{deliverables}}.
Evaluate completion using: {{completionChecks}}.
Pause for my review at: {{checkpoints}}.
Explain any material uncertainty or failed check. Do not report completion without the deliverables and the results of those checks.

source.section: Three Ways to Work with AI

title: Ask for a concrete challenge
purpose: Get useful objections to an idea rather than general praise.
text:
Review this proposal: {{proposal}}.
The context is {{context}} and the criteria are {{criteria}}.
Identify specific weaknesses, assumptions that need evidence, and circumstances in which the proposal could fail. Explain which claims you can assess from the information supplied and which you cannot. Suggest the most useful next check. Do not infer that the proposal is good because I wrote it.

title: Learn with hints
purpose: Keep the learner attempting the work.
text:
Help me learn {{skill}}. My present understanding is {{currentUnderstanding}}. Use this practice problem: {{practiceProblem}}.
Begin by asking what I would try. Offer a small hint when needed and let me attempt the next step before giving more help. Ask me to explain my reasoning. Afterward, give me a different problem to attempt without your solution. If your explanation depends on facts you cannot verify, flag that limitation.

title: Look from another perspective
purpose: Find plausible objections without pretending simulated people are real participants.
text:
Consider this proposal: {{proposal}}.
Known context: {{knownContext}}.
Use these perspectives to identify different concerns: {{relevantPerspectives}}.
For each, list a plausible objection and the evidence needed to investigate it. Treat these as hypotheses for me to check with real people or sources. Do not present simulated reactions as observations or predict actual people’s choices with certainty.

source.section: When You Need a Different Perspective
